To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CR MAC protocols in overlay mode are more mature than those in underlay mode; the centralized CR MAC protocols can achieve higher spectrum utilization efficiency; and the distributed CR MAC can achieve better performance in terms of spectrum utilization efficiency and fairness.

The medium access control ( MAC ) protocols in cognitive radio (CR ) networks play a crucial role to exploit the available spectrum opportunities, manage interference to primary users, and coordinate spectrum access amongst secondary (unlicensed) users.

1) the design and implementation challenges of the CR MAC protocols include the spectrum sharing mode, architecture, and sharing behaviors; 2) the CR MAC protocols in the underlay mode could achieve higher spectrum utilization efficiency, but with the cost of complicated power and admission controls; and 3) the centralized CR MAC protocols can be used to do spectrum sensing in the quiet period of whole networks, while the distributed MAC protocols are more applicable to the dynamic spectrum access.
